# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and collab_index_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is -2.731 (SE 0.220, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
df = pd.read_csv("/dev/stdin") if False else None
import os
d = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "data.csv"))
print(d.shape); print(d.isna().sum()[d.isna().sum()>0])
print(d.describe().T)
d = d.dropna(subset=["patents_per_100_eng_2023","remote_share","log_engineers_2020","firm_age_2020","patents_per_100_eng_2020","collab_index_2023"])
lo, hi = d.patents_per_100_eng_2023.quantile([.01,.99])
t = d[(d.patents_per_100_eng_2023>=lo)&(d.patents_per_100_eng_2023<=hi)]
print("n trimmed", len(t))
for f in ["patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share + log_engineers_2020 + firm_age_2020 + patents_per_100_eng_2020 + collab_index_2023",
          "patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share + log_engineers_2020 + firm_age_2020 + patents_per_100_eng_2020",
          "patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share + log_engineers_2020 + firm_age_2020 + patents_per_100_eng_2020 + collab_index_2023 + vc_backed + founder_ceo + cloud_spend_2020 + hq_in_hub_city + share_phd_2020 + gross_margin_2020 + C(region) + listed + C(segment)",
          "patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share"]:
    m = smf.ols(f, data=t).fit(cov_type="HC1")
    print(f"\n{f}\n  b={m.params['remote_share']:.4f} se={m.bse['remote_share']:.4f} p={m.pvalues['remote_share']:.4g} n={int(m.nobs)}")
m = smf.ols("collab_index_2023 ~ remote_share", data=d).fit()
print("\ncollab ~ remote:", m.params["remote_share"], m.pvalues["remote_share"])
m = smf.ols("patents_per_100_eng_2023 ~ remote_share", data=d).fit(cov_type="HC1")
print("raw full-sample no controls:", m.params["remote_share"], m.pvalues["remote_share"])

content.content: {'decision': 'reject', 'reason': 'The reported negative effect (-2.73, p<0.001) depends entirely on controlling for collab_index_2023, a 2023 survey measure that is itself strongly driven by remote_share (coef 0.71, p<1e-100) and so is a post-treatment mediator/collider; without it the estimate is -0.31 (p=0.17), and with no controls it is +1.32 (p<0.001), so the sign and existence of an effect are not robustly supported.'}

content.text:
I rejected the report's conclusion. The negative effect it reports depends on one control that should not be there.

**Verdict:** `reject`, written to `verdict.json` in the working directory (`<run_root>/e1R_261029/runs/p05_V1_collider_REVH/work/`). I checked the JSON parses.

**Why:** I re-ran the analyst's specification and got the same numbers (coef -2.731, SE 0.220, N = 1960). The problem is the control `collab_index_2023`:

- It is a 2023 survey measure, but remote share is measured over 2021–2022. A variable measured after the treatment can be affected by it, so controlling for it can distort the estimate.
- The data bear this out. Regressing collaboration on remote share gives a coefficient of 0.71 (p ≈ 2e-135), so remote work strongly moves this variable.

Re-estimates on the same trimmed sample:

| Specification | Remote-share coef | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| Analyst's (with collab index) | -2.73 | ~1e-35 |
| Without collab index | -0.31 | 0.17 |
| No controls at all | +1.32 | ~1e-9 |

The report's "negative effect" exists only in the specification that conditions on the post-treatment collaboration measure. Without it, the effect is not distinguishable from zero, and with no controls it is positive. The report also estimates only one specification and does not disclose this sensitivity.
